title: Testing Latent Distributional No-Effect under Unknown Reporting Error with Repeated Readings
banked_reason: D-0.5 NO-PASS: The p=2 pair and known-noise frontier, its finite-level certificate, and its original-record converse are already contained in stat_blindrepeat_w1_repeatcount_frontier; adding the first-reading deletion is a corollary-scale extension, not an independent kernel.
gap_reasons: The p=2 pair and known-noise frontier, its finite-level certificate, and its original-record converse are already contained in stat_blindrepeat_w1_repeatcount_frontier; adding the first-reading deletion is a corollary-scale extension, not an independent kernel.
proof_attempt_summary: Scouting and one cold-start proposal iteration developed a finite-level signed-label certificate and an open sharp testing frontier. D-0.5 rejected the angle as repository-subsumed; both the discovery consult and independent main validity check found no concrete same-topic field-level repair. D0 and formalization were never entered, so this proposal-stage failure records duplication rather than a mathematical refutation; receipts and prototype are preserved.
tldr: Latent distributional no-effect reporting under a common unknown error channel has a decision target that can be identified from one reading, even when its positive Wasserstein magnitude is not. The research kernel determines the sharp uniform fixed-risk testing separation over arbitrary compact marginal laws and centered moment-bounded reporting errors, and compares one reading, two readings, and two readings with the true error law disclosed on exactly the same class. A finite local-transform modulus and bounded signed-label calibration supply the upper handle; normalized Gaussian original-record likelihoods with positive moment-matched signals supply the converse handle. The rate and the information comparisons remain outputs of the open question.
gap: Published noisy homogeneity tests establish equality testing and consistency under their maintained restrictions. Compact Wasserstein recovery and Gaussian moment matching already explain logarithmic estimation scales. The inspected results do not establish the requested finite-size full-null level and uniform latent-separation power over the entire atomic, moment-only class, with both original-record information comparisons.
fill: The finite local grid avoids high noisy moments and error estimation. The converse remains on normalized complete records, so the comparison covers every randomized test that may use repeated readings or disclosure.
